public_rationale: AP announced on July 13, 2023 that OpenAI was licensing part of its text archive [e7]. OpenAI's December 13, 2023 Axel Springer announcement included use of the publisher's content for model training [e8]. These agreements establish licensing activity before January 8, 2024 and support the factual claim that licensing selected content was an available option known to OpenAI [e7, e8]. They do not establish the accusation of knowing dishonesty or the feasibility of licensing an entire training corpus [e7, e8].
limitations: The supported assessment covers the factual licensing proposition; the agreements do not establish private beliefs or intent to deceive [e7, e8].
Selected agreements do not establish the cost or commercial feasibility of licensing all desired training content [e7, e8].

our_interpretation: The checkable factual core is that OpenAI had pursued or signed content-licensing agreements before the post, demonstrating institutional awareness that licensing was possible.
Have been describes activity preceding publication, with no stated starting date. The target period therefore ends on 2024-01-08 and has an unspecified beginning.
The accusation of knowing dishonesty goes beyond the observable existence of deals and is not established merely by verifying them.
This is a claim about the existence of licensing arrangements, not their price, profitability, or accounting treatment.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable pre-post records show OpenAI pursuing or signing content-licensing agreements.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that the alleged licensing activity did not occur. A lack of public announcements alone would not suffice.
